notes: The parts are the same as in step 1, with no additions or removals.
The circuit image is the authority. Red goes from the Yún 5V header pin to the TMP36 +Vs row. Yellow goes from A1 to the TMP36 Vout row. Black goes from GND to the TMP36 GND row. The sketch reads A1.
The schematic labels the sensor output as A0, but the image and the text both use A1, so I followed A1.

The sensor is a TMP36 in a TO-92 package. Pin 1 is +Vs, pin 2 is Vout and pin 3 is GND. It sits in three adjacent 5-hole strips of the mini breadboard, and each jumper wire goes into the same strip as its sensor leg.
The breadboard is drawn rotated in the image. The strip names 8t, 9t and 10t are my choice of columns. The wire end is in row a and the sensor leg in row e of each strip.
The sketch also describes using A0 and A2 as software power and ground pins. The image does not wire them, so I did not add them.
The micro-SD card is only inserted in the Yún's slot. The headers variant of the Yún has no port for that slot, so the edge has no ports.
